newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rail workers end strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rail workers end strike.

text.p: The loss-making state railways (HZ) and a striking railworkers' union on Thursday reached an agreement to end a wage dispute, state television (HRT) reported.

The union halted all freight traffic on December 28, only days after calling off a three-week strike by 11,000 workers that had paralysed traffic across the country. The first stoppage was ruled illegal by the Supreme Court.
HRT said HZ agreed to sign the first part of a collective agreement guaranteeing higher wages for rail workers.
"If the tariff part of the agreement is not reached by April 30, HZ agrees to provide extra money...so to ensure a fair distribution of wages among the employed," the HRT said.
The government previously refused to give in to workers' demands, saying there was no money to increase pay this year.
The railway company received more than one billion kuna ($200 million) from the 1996 budget, but the government wants to keep the subsidy below that.
HRT said parliament is due to discuss restructuring the company and find a long-term solution for its problem.
Newspapers reported that railway tickets would increase by up to 52 percent for long-distance travel from January 1.
